meta.scene_summary: We're building the future of AI while the present is busy setting the server room on fire.

cooking.headline: Google just dropped Genie 4, as if we didn't have enough tabs open already
cooking.summary: Google released a new version of their generative world model, because clearly, the only thing missing from our lives was another AI to keep us distracted. It is the perfect tool for when you want to avoid fixing that one lingering production bug for another few hours.
cooking.plain_english: Google has launched Genie 4, which is a new artificial intelligence model capable of generating interactive virtual environments.

cooked.headline: Turns out 'let AI handle the deployments' was just a fancy way to say 'let's break everything at once.'
cooked.summary: Bank CEOs and the NSA are finally admitting that letting AI push patches to critical infrastructure is like handing a toddler the keys to a Ferrari. It turns out that when you automate chaos, you don't get efficiency; you just get a really fast way to crash the global economy.
cooked.plain_english: Bank leaders and intelligence officials stated that recent banking system outages were caused by automated artificial intelligence software updates.

cooked.headline: Nginx just dropped a remote code execution vulnerability that makes 'move fast and break things' look polite.
cooked.summary: There is a new remote code execution vulnerability in Nginx, which is essentially the digital equivalent of leaving your front door wide open while inviting the whole internet inside. It's the perfect time to remind everyone that your web server is only as secure as the last patch you ignored.
cooked.plain_english: A critical security flaw has been discovered in Nginx that allows unauthorized attackers to remotely execute malicious code on affected servers.

cooked.headline: When your reverse proxy decides to become the landlord
cooked.summary: NGINX is supposed to be the bouncer at the door, but this exploit lets visitors walk right into the server's basement and start rearranging the furniture. It turns out the most secure way to handle web traffic is to just hope nobody finds the trapdoor in your configuration.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability in the NGINX web server software allows an attacker to gain full administrative control over the host system.

cooked.headline: Java's Base64 decoder is having a rough week
cooked.summary: Java's latest trick is turning a simple Base64 string into a remote code execution vulnerability, proving that even basic data processing can be a total landmine. It is the digital equivalent of trying to read a postcard and accidentally granting the mailman power of attorney over your house.
cooked.plain_english: A flaw in the Java development kit allows unauthorized code execution when the software processes certain types of encoded data.

cooked.headline: KVM just found out that sometimes you need to actually clear your cache
cooked.summary: A security patch just landed for KVM because it was failing to reset the MMU context when emulating an INIT signal. It turns out that carrying over stale state during a system reset is a great way to let attackers play tag with your memory.
cooked.plain_english: A vulnerability in the Linux kernel's virtual machine software has been fixed to ensure memory settings are properly cleared when a virtual computer restarts.

cooked.headline: Hackers are using A/B testing to see if your computer prefers malware
cooked.summary: Attackers hijacked Optimizely to run A/B tests on malicious payloads to see which versions tricked the most users. It's the ultimate growth hacking nightmare where the conversion metric is how many people you successfully infect.
cooked.plain_english: Cybercriminals used a legitimate website testing service to experiment with different versions of malware to determine which ones were most effective at infecting users.

cooked.headline: Waymo is officially banned from California freeways
cooked.summary: California regulators decided that autonomous cars need to stay off the highway, effectively putting them on a permanent learner's permit. It turns out that teaching a robot to merge in LA traffic is the ultimate 'do not try this at home' project.
cooked.plain_english: California has prohibited Waymo's self-driving vehicles from operating on state freeways.

cooked.headline: Nvidia board says Jensen Huang is not getting his job back
cooked.summary: The board has officially confirmed they aren't looking to rehire their former CEO, which is a classic 'we've moved on' energy. It's like breaking up with your partner and then having them check your LinkedIn profile every single day to see if you're hiring.
cooked.plain_english: Nvidia's board of directors stated they do not intend to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO.

cooked.headline: AI coding agents have officially turned us all into full-time code reviewers
cooked.summary: Researchers found that AI agents are great at writing code, they just forgot to mention that you now have to spend your entire day babysitting their hallucinations. It turns out the promised automation just shifted the bottleneck from typing to reading someone else's messy work.
cooked.plain_english: A study by Harvard researchers indicates that while AI tools speed up the initial writing of code, they create a new delay by requiring humans to spend more time reviewing and correcting the AI's output.
